key_insight: The paper shows that training loss depends jointly on learning-rate and batch-size schedules, and derives a closed-form optimal batch-size schedule for any chosen learning-rate schedule.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical recipe for dynamic batch-size scheduling that can improve large-model training efficiency beyond static batch-size baselines.
method: Model training dynamics using a convex-optimization lens.
Derive a joint loss characterization in terms of learning-rate and batch-size schedules.
Use this characterization to obtain closed-form optimal batch-size schedules and joint scaling laws.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the proposed joint scaling laws consistently outperform static batch-size baselines.
watch_item: The closed-form schedule still needs careful integration with real training systems, since optimizer, hardware, and memory constraints may limit how freely batch size can vary.
paper_title: Towards joint scaling laws with optimal batch size schedules
